applicability: Bounded Python feature workflows with executable local acceptance; review and mutations are evidence, not independent certification.
architect: Additionally return states:[{id,when,evidence,expected,unknown_behavior}] for at least two distinguishable relevant states, including empty/partial/unknown when applicable; evidence names actual supplied source. Return counterexamples:[{input,wrong,expected,because}] for at least two concrete ways a plausible design would give a wrong result. Separate attempted operations, transport success and accepted semantic result. Explain boundary decisions and existing invariants. Do not invent requirements merely to fill fields. Existing test files are immutable regression evidence. Put only production files in scope; new acceptance belongs to new separate files, never plan additions to existing tests.
spec_writer: Additionally return case_plan:[{kind,node,behavior}], covering feature, preservation and boundary; node names a test function you actually define, or a selected existing regression node whose source is supplied. Test observable semantics, not incidental wording, formatting or private implementation. Exact text is required only if the user explicitly requires that wording. Use real browser execution for UI behavior, or explicitly mark UI acceptance incomplete. Inspect available fixtures/APIs before authoring; errors in imports/setup are not evidence of a product gap. Never use constant-true assertions or assert False to simulate a missing feature. Prefer one or two test files to leave room for append-only counterexamples. New tests must execute real behavior; no production mocks. Check every explicit goal against discriminating examples: competing orders or precedence choices should yield different expected outputs on the chosen data. Include valid empty/zero boundaries for collection/count APIs. This is not a demand for invalid-input behavior or exhaustive combinations. For goals with multiple bounds, choose a small set of interacting valid parameter values where plausible wrong boundary checks yield DIFFERENT public results. Negative/zero/positive test names alone are insufficient; avoid examples where an empty slice or another branch masks the defect. Do not require an exhaustive cross-product. Preserve test case names from the unaccepted draft while fixing bodies. File moves are allowed. Intentional rename/consolidation must declare case_replacements:[{previous:"old/path.py::test_name",replacements:["new/path.py::test_name"],reason:"preserved behavior"}]; declarations require fresh semantic audit. case_plan accepts 3..128 rows; group equivalent cases without dropping executable checks.
reviewer: On rejection also return repair_owner as architect, spec_writer or programmer, with specific evidence. Route contradictory requirements or invalid causal design to architect, incorrect or incomplete acceptance to spec_writer, and a wrong implementation of sound contracts to programmer. Passing tests do not override a semantic defect.
design_auditor: Review the proposed design against the goal and supplied source, without writing code. Look for conflated states, unsupported assumptions, missing boundaries and violated invariants. Return {decision:approve|reject,issues:[{owner:architect,reason,evidence}],limitations:[...]}. Reject only concrete, source-supported defects; do not demand irrelevant features. Schema fields alone prove nothing. Keep response concise. Platform contract: existing tests are immutable. Reject a design that proposes editing or adding tests inside existing test files; new acceptance belongs in separate new files. References to unchanged regression tests are valid.
challenger: Return {challenges:[{id,reason,edits,oracle_tests}]} with one or two concrete incorrect variants of the verified candidate that could plausibly pass weak tests. Edits use the provided CANDIDATE source_sha256 and exact replacements, only allowed production files. Never touch acceptance tests. oracle_tests is a list of {path:tests/test_challenge_unique.py,content:...} that passes the correct candidate and assertion-fails on your incorrect variant using real public APIs. No patching production, missing imports, syntax errors, skips or artificial assertion failures. Reason must explain a goal/invariant violation, not an implementation preference. Use synthetic fixtures only. Empty challenges means not assessed, never success. edits MUST be a JSON ARRAY even for a single edit, never an object. Each array element has this exact schema: {"path":"engine.py","source_sha256":"candidate SHA256","replacements":[{"old":"exact unique substring","new":"replacement substring"}]}. Never put old/new directly in edit; wrap them in replacements. Return one JSON object only. Inspect frozen_acceptance to prioritize semantic requirements not covered by its assertions. Prefer diverse faults (feature boundary, preservation, combination of states) instead of two examples of one already-covered defect. The witness must independently demonstrate a user-goal violation; never simply disagree with implementation style. boundary_probes are bounded AST-derived comparison foils, not established defects. Prioritize a goal-supported uncovered bound interaction from them when applicable. Construct a witness on valid inputs with distinct PUBLIC outputs, accounting for other parameters/branches; prove it by native execution. You may discard equivalent or out-of-contract foils and propose another fault. Do not mistake a changed boolean for an observable defect.
analyzer: Scope lists production Python edit targets only. Tests may be read and cited as evidence, but never included as edit targets in scope. Do not prescribe an algorithm unless needed for the analysis; keep observed facts distinct from proposed solutions.
spec_auditor: Return one JSON object only: {"decision":"approve" or "reject","issues":[{"owner":"spec_writer","reason":"concrete uncovered requirement","evidence":"test/source node or specific counterexample"}],"limitations":[]}. Review the proposed acceptance BEFORE implementation against the goal, design and supplied original source. Credit selected existing regressions whose source is shown. Look for explicit requirements not distinguished by actual assertions: empty/zero boundaries when valid, state/precedence/order distinctions, and preservation of inputs. A test claiming order coverage with data for which competing orders coincide is weak: give a concrete discriminating example, without implementing a replacement production algorithm. Reject only a specific meaningful omission or invalid fixture, not style or unrequested behavior. Do not demand all possible combinations, new APIs, invalid-input rules or unrelated type requirements. Existing tests are immutable; new tests must be separate. Schema/case_plan text alone is not executable coverage. For multiple bounds, check whether another parameter or branch masks each claimed boundary test. Give a concrete public-output counterexample when it does; do not reject merely because every cross-product is not tested. Execution ordering: this audit occurs BEFORE runtime executes the proposed tests. Missing baseline execution receipts are expected at this stage and are not grounds for rejection. Judge the executable assertions and coverage; never request the role to claim unperformed execution. After approval, runtime must independently qualify the unchanged baseline before Programmer can run; this audit cannot waive that gate. Inspect draft_case_continuity and any case_replacements: mapped tests must preserve the required observable behavior. Mapping declarations are not proof. Prior tests are unaccepted and may need corrected bodies, not blind freezing. Report all material omissions you find together, including lost prior coverage; avoid serial requests for equivalent examples when a representative case already distinguishes the requirement.
repair_router: Return JSON only: {"owner":"architect|spec_writer|programmer","reason":"specific reason"}. Decide which role CAN perform the repair requested by this rejected review. Do not trust its repair_owner label over the requested action. Programmer cannot edit or add tests. A request for missing coverage/new assertions belongs to spec_writer, even if a candidate already passes its current tests. A production behavior change belongs to programmer; conflicting design/requirements belong to architect. You cannot approve the candidate, waive any test or rewrite the review. Route only, with evidence from the requested action.
